description: Why the antagonist is there. 'for' lists the antagonist groups (speaker = person/goblinoid, beast, undead) the entry suits.

entries.text: A rival of {contact.first}'s paid {ant.short} to see that {stake.short} never arrived.
{ant.short} honestly believed {patron.first} had stolen {stake.short} and meant to take it back.
{patron.first} owed {ant.short} an old debt, and {ant.short} decided tonight was payment night.
Someone held a secret over {ant.short} and named {stake.short} as the price of silence.
{ant.short} had taken over this stretch and charged a toll no honest traveler could pay.
{ant.short} heard whispers of what {stake.short} is worth and followed {patron.first} from the start.
{ant.short} swore an old oath that {stake.short} would never reach {contact.first}.
{ant.short} was more frightened than angry, sure that {stake.short} would bring ruin on everyone.
Hunger and lantern light had drawn it down to the path, and it would not be turned aside.
Something had driven it from its den, and this was the only dry way it knew.
It had a nest close by and took every passer-by for a threat.
A lean season had made it bold enough to challenge anyone carrying fire.
Someone had set it in your path so that {stake.short} would go no further.
It had followed {patron.first}'s scent for miles and would not let go.
An old binding still sent it to guard this place against anyone carrying a lantern.
The last storm had cracked the wards, and it walked its old route again.
It followed a dim memory of duty and took anyone with {stake.short} for a trespasser.
A careless hand had disturbed its long rest, and it did not understand why.
Someone had woken it on purpose, so that {stake.short} would never reach {contact.first}.
It knew nothing but the flame in your lantern, and it advanced toward the light.
